scenario: A regional bank's internal loan database only records loans above $50,000 â€” smaller personal loans are handled by a third-party servicer and are not in the main system. A risk analyst uses the internal database to estimate the bank's average loan size for capital planning.

data.description: Internal database includes only loans > $50,000. Loan sizes assumed Normal with known standard deviation Ïƒ = $30,000.

question: The internal database reports a mean loan size of $85,000. Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean loan size Î¼ across all loans the bank originates (including those below $50,000), and (b) the fraction of all loans that are recorded in the internal database.
naive_answer: The true mean loan size is approximately $85,000 since that is the database average.
naive_trap: The database excludes all loans under $50,000. The true mean is about $11,000 lower. The fraction of loans below the threshold (about 21%) represents a meaningful portion of origination volume that the analyst is ignoring.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(50000-mu)/30000; sf=norm.sf(a); return mu+30000*norm.pdf(a)/sf-85000 if sf>1e-10 else 1e10
mu=brentq(eq,1000,84999)
assert abs(mu-73953)<500
assert abs(norm.sf((50000-mu)/30000)-0.7877)<0.005
